top.title: Oyo’ll no longer depend on oil, raw materials for economic prosperity – Makinde
top.description: …state targets global market for arts, crafts By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has declared its determination to move beyond dependence on conventional sources of revenue by harnessing the economic potential of arts, crafts, cultural festivals, and tourism to generate foreign exchange, attract international investments, and create employment opportunities. The government said it was working to transform Nigeria’s rich cultural heritage into commercially viable products for the global export market, positioning the creative economy as a major driver of economic growth and sustainable development. The initiative, which sought to unlock the enormous economic value of indigenous artistic expressions, traditional knowledge, and cultural assets, will be driven through the Oyo State Business Forum 2026, with the theme “Investment and Export Promotion of Arts and Crafts Business in Oyo State.” The forum is expected to bring together investors, artists, craftsmen, exporters, policymakers, and development partners to explore investment opportunities, strengthen export capacity, and expand the international market for Nigerian arts and crafts. Speaking at a press briefing to announce the forum, the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Dr. Wasiu Olatubosun, said the administration of Governor Seyi Makinde was deliberately repositioning culture beyond its traditional function as a custodian of heritage to become a productive economic sector capable of generating wealth, attracting investments, and contributing meaningfully to national development. Olatubosun, who spoke at the briefing organized in collaboration with the Oyo State Investment and Public-Private Partnership Agency (OYSIPA) at the state Secretariat, Ibadan, described Nigeria’s cultural wealth as an enormous but largely untapped economic resource that could compete favorably in the international marketplace. He maintained that traditional festivals, indigenous knowledge, artistic expressions, and locally produced crafts possessed considerable commercial value and could become major export commodities if properly researched, documented, developed, and marketed. According to him, the state government is also repositioning its cultural festivals from routine annual celebrations into internationally competitive tourism and entertainment products capable of attracting foreign visitors, investors, and members of the African diaspora. He identified the recent inscription of the Sango Festival on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as a major boost to Oyo State’s international cultural standing and an opportunity to attract greater global attention. The commissioner explained that the recognition had taken the annual festival in Oyo Town beyond its traditional geographical and cultural boundaries, making it an increasingly attractive destination for international tourists, cultural enthusiasts, and media organizations from Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

top.title: Georgetown keeps playoff streak alive: Clutch win earns Eagles 12th straight postseason
top.description: The last time Georgetown football missed the UIL playoffs, the first Apple Watch had just debuted and NFL superstar Patrick Mahomes was still an underclassman at Texas Tech. And thanks to running back Zechariah Guyton, the Eagles will continue their streak. Georgetown (6-4, 5-3) rode three touchdowns from Guyton to a 28-14 win over Killeen that cemented the Eagles' place in the postseason Friday at Birkelbach Field. With three wins in their final four games of the regular season, the Eagles rose to third place in District 12-5A Division I and qualified for the playoffs for the 12th consecutive year. MORE: Cedar Ridge defeats Round Rock in thriller Georgetown head coach Chuck Griffin meets Rouse head coach Joshua Mann after the game at John Gumption Stadium on Thursday, Oct. 10, 2024 in Cedar Park, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/American-Statesman) Guyton recorded Georgetown's first points of the night with a 1-yard touchdown run with 2 minutes, 13 seconds left in the first quarter. The power back also muscled his way into the end zone for the 2-point conversion to make the score 8-0. Those were the only points until the Kangaroos (5-5, 4-4) cut the deficit to one point on a 39-yard passing touchdown with 6:46 left in the third quarter. Georgetown tacked on a safety and a 26-yard field goal from Dan Lopez to extend the lead to 13-7 before the third period ended. Georgetown added two more touchdowns from Guyton in the fourth, while Killeen also found the end zone again. MORE: Hutto thumps Vandegrift in Central Texas high school football matchup The Eagles were on the outside looking in for the postseason just two weeks ago. But an Oct. 23 win at A&M Consolidated buoyed Georgetown into the top four of the district standings and Friday's win, coupled with Consol's loss to Hendrickson, pushed Georgetown up to third. Next for the Eagles is a bi-district matchup with Angleton (9-1), which has averaged 47.6 points this season while barely allowing more than 10 per game. top.title: Browns season heading into Week 9 versus the Saints: Ahead of schedule good enough?
top.description: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Going into the season, the expectations around the Cleveland Browns were reasonably low . New coaching staff, the youngest roster in the league, uncertainty at the quarterback position, and the team just traded one of the best defensive players of this generation to Inglewood . Fast forward to early November, the Browns are 5-3 and are still in the playoff hunt in the AFC . Considering how many believed that around this time Cleveland would be in “making mock drafts” territory ( Editor’s Note: I did create one recently , just one), 5-3 is better than what anyone thought. As people will question how good the Browns are, it’s a fair process to go through. However, in this day and age, context is rarely used correctly. Going into the season, Cleveland had one of the easier schedules. In the first 8 games of the season, the Browns were only favored in 1 of their 5 wins, their most recent one: Week 2 @ Buccaneers: 23-19 Week 3 vs Panthers: 21-18 Week 4 vs Steelers: 27-24 Week 6 vs Ravens: 13-10 Week 7 @ Titans: 27-24 Fans’ confidence in the team has waxed and waned throughout the season, but is higher than it was before the season. If you want to argue which win was most impressive, you can make an argument that it was the home win against the Steelers. The final score doesn’t indicate how the game actually went. If you rewatched that game, the Browns looked like the better team throughout, and it was a surprise to everyone watching that night. Winning in the NFL is hard, and it doesn’t matter how you do it. Is Cleveland a good football team? Bad football team? Neither. Average, so far, but young. Offensively, despite their issues, they are better than last year. Having better personnel helps, but the scheme is better than last season. Defensively, the unit isn’t as dominant as last season, but it’s still regarded as one of the better units in the NFL. Progress is being shown even if the results aren’t as impressive. If the team were winless or 1-7, we would argue that the Browns are making any progress at all. Instead, the team is 5-3 and exceeding expectations. It’s possible that the team goes over their win total sooner rather than later , and it’s possible that the team is playing meaningful games towards mid-November and early December. top.title: Bronny James Opens Up On Playing In The G League After Impressive Season Debut
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images The 2026-27 G League season got underway on Friday, and the Coachella Valley Lakers got a big boost ahead of their opener against the Salt Lake City Stars at Acrisure Arena. The Los Angeles Lakers assigned Bronny James and Cameron Carr to the G League , and they helped take down the Stars 104-98. James impressed on the night and expressed satisfaction with the team’s performance postgame . “I think we played well, played together,” James said, via The Sporting Tribune. “We’re definitely locked in on the defensive end, and that helped us in the second half and the fourth quarter especially. So I think we did our job right, and came away with the win.” The Lakers forced the Stars into 21 turnovers and really stepped up defensively after the first quarter. The visitors only managed 19 points in the second quarter and 22 in the third. This helped the Lakers take a 76-68 lead into the fourth quarter, but the Stars roared back in the final period and even took a 94-93 lead with 2:27 remaining. It looked like the Coachella Valley era might get off to a losing start for the hosts, but they then tightened things up. They closed the game on an 11-4 run to get off to a 1-0 start in this Tip-Off Tournament before the regular season. James, the No. 55 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, finished with 22 points (8-18 FG), five rebounds, seven assists, and one steal against the Stars. The 22-year-old was a lot more aggressive than he is in the NBA, but claimed that his mindset does not change. “Just playing my game,” James said. “The same way I’d gone with two minutes left or whatever with the Lakers. Just trying to play smart and be aggressive.” That’s all James had been getting in the NBA. He was averaging 0.8 points and 0.2 blocks in 2.4 minutes per game. While some might look at a G League demotion negatively, James is happy to get the opportunity to play. “I love playing a game of basketball and to be able to come down here and actually produce is good for me and good for my spirit,” James said. “And whenever I’m called down here or whatever, I’m all open to coming down here and playing.” Sitting on the bench isn’t going to help James develop. He needs to play, and that was the message that Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick sent to him and Carr . “The messaging was very simple. It’s just: you guys need reps, and you guys need to play,” Redick said, via Benjamin Royer. Carr put up 13 points (5-11 FG) and four rebounds against the Stars. He had gone down with a right oblique strain in preseason and definitely could do with playing extended minutes to find his footing. James and Carr head back to the Los Angeles Lakers now, but they might be spending a fair bit of time in the G League this season. It’s a new beginning for their affiliate, as they relocated from El Segundo to the Coachella Valley in the offseason.

top.title: Rutgers Guard Kwabena Asamoah to Miss the Rest of the Season with Injury
top.description: PISCATAWAY, NJ - NOVEMBER 19: Rutgers Scarlet Knights offensive lineman Kwabena Asamoah (69) during the college football game between the Rutgers Scarlet Knights and the Penn State Nittany Lions on November 19, 2022 at SHI Stadium in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Rutgers Star guard Kwabena Asamoah will miss the rest of the season due to surgery he had for a high ankle sprain, according to 247Sports’ Bobby Deren. Asamoah, who chose to return to Rutgers for his fifth year, has played in 48 total games for the program. Unortantely due to the injury, he played his last game in a Scarlet Knight uniform as he is now out of eligibility. According to multiple reports, he is expected to make a full recovery and continue football training in January so that he is ready for the NFL Draft. Asamoah achieved several notable accolades during his Rutgers career, including being named team captain in 2026, being an All-Big Ten honorable mention in 2024 and 2025, as well as earning second-team All-America by ESPN in 2025. He also cleared the way for three 1,000-yard rushers during his career, blocking for Kyle Monangai and Antwan Raymond, who rushed for over 1,000 yards in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Through eight games of 2026, Asamoah played 498 snaps at right guard. Over that time, he allowed only three total pressures, which is tied for the fourth-fewest in the country among guards who have played at least 400 snaps. His list of consecutive starts was one of the longest on the team, as he started every game in 2024, 2025, and the first eight games in 2026. With his college career now over, Asamoah will look to recover quickly and prepare for the NFL Draft. In addition to Asamoah being ruled out for the season, star wide receiver KJ Duff has been ruled out for the Knights’ upcoming game against Wisconsin. His injury has been deemed a lower-body injury, but specifics have not been released. Last week, Duff left the game against Michigan early due to the injury. These two, combined with starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan being out for the game, mean that Rutgers will be taking on Wisconsin without several key pieces on offense.

But the delay in a Downs deal is apparently due to the Colts looking for a team that can meet their asking price. As reported by ESPN’s Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter, the Colts have been telling teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for Downs. It remains to be seen whether the Colts are being truthful about that fourth-round offer being on the table as they look to bump up the price for Downs. If they are, then Downs is as good as gone before the trade deadline. top.title: Tottenham dealt latest attacking injury blow after VAR madness at Leeds
top.description: Tottenham have been dealt another attacking injury blow after Mathys Tel limped off before half-time against Leeds . Tel was unable to continue after being on the end of a stamp by Jayden Bogle, who caught the Frenchman on the ankle with his studs. VAR spent over four minutes reviewing the incident to determine whether it was a red card offence, only for referee John Brooks - who didn’t even caution Bogle initially - to be told to stick with the on-field decision. This meant the right wing-back got away with the challenge scot free. “The referee’s call of no red card to Bogle for the challenge on Tel was checked and confirmed by VAR,” said the Premier League Match Centre. Should Jason Bogle have seen red for this challenge? 🟥👀 📺 Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/fuK42Okkcz — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 7, 2026 The statement added VAR Tony Harrington’s verdict to Brooks: “I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge”. The challenge was similar to the one that saw Jean-Philippe Mateta shown red after a VAR review when Spurs played Crystal Palace last weekend. Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi was visibly frustrated with the outcome of the review and expressed his displeasure again when Pedro Porro was booked for a similar foul after the break, with the Italian booked for his reaction. Roberto De Zerbi was booked for his reaction after Pedro Porro was cautioned for a similar tackle to Jayden Bogle’s (Reuters) “Pedro Porro's was a duel and an incredible yellow card. The first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing,” De Zerbi told TNT Sports , before stopping short of criticising the officials. Asked if the referee should have gone to the monitor to review Bogle’s challenge, he said: "No. I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor. If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve." De Zerbi’s woes were exacerbated when Tel signalled to the bench that he would need to come off, having tried to play through the pain for five minutes. Tel was replaced by Dominic Solanke in the 43rd minute, who was dropped from the starting line-up following the Palace win. top.title: Maryvale football wins first playoff game in 21 years
top.description: For the first time in 21 years, the Maryvale Panthers have won a playoff game. No. 13 Phoenix Maryvale shut out the No. 20 ALA West Foothills Guardians, 35-0, in a first-round 4A high school football playoff game on Friday, Nov. 6. The Panthers used a stifling defense to secure three takeaways and consistently give the offense a short field. Key Plays The Panthers scored their first touchdown of the game when freshman quarterback Marcus Escobedo Jr. found Miles Woods for a 14-yard score with 5:16 to go in the first. Maryvale junior running back Isaac Buchanan scored the first of his two touchdowns after a 25-yard run reached pay dirt with 7:15 to go in the second quarter. Escobedo Jr. found the end zone after a nifty red zone scramble and crossed the pylon with just seconds before the first half ended, putting the Panthers up 21-0. Buchanan scored the final touchdown of the game scoring from a yard out after a 35-yard catch and run from Woods set them up with a goal to go at the 1 yardline. Key Players Maryvale's Escobedo Jr. finished the game throwing for 209 yards and a touchdown on 11 of 15 passing. He also added a rushing touchdown. Woods caught five passes for 135 yards and a touchdown, averaging a whopping 27 yards a catch in Friday's contest. Junior RB Buchanan had a workhorse performance rushing for 67 yards on 16 carries and scoring two touchdowns. Quotes "Tonight we blanked a really good football team," Maryvale co-head coach Marcus Carter said. "We're physical, we're fast, we're young and these kids are sponges and they're hungry. To pitch a shutout against a really good ALA west team is a statement." "Our freshman QB has poise," Maryvale co-head coach Mark Carter said. "He could have gone to any school, he decided to come here, we feel blessed to have him and he's only going to get better." "We just couldn't get that spark," ALA West Foothill head coach Bryan Rauzen said. "We're going to miss these seniors a lot but I can positively say we are building a tradition here." Up next Maryvale (10-1) will travel to Prescott, to face No. 4 Bradshaw Mountain (7-3) in the second round on Nov. 13. The Bears had a first-round bye. The season ended Friday for ALA West Foothills. top.description: MLS winners and losers GFX - GOAL A points record within reach, seasons on the brink and star names under pressure: GOAL’s writers debate who will rise - and who could fall - on MLS Decision Day. Right, so, Decision Day time. For those uninitiated, this is basically where all of the MLS games kick off at the same time on the final day of the regular season. In an ideal world, there are still loads of possible permutations and combinations as to who makes the playoffs and how. Decision Day is supposed to be, well, decisive. And this year, it might just be lacking a bit of spark. The East, from a 'who makes it' POV is sewn up. The West has a little wildcard jeopardy, but basically we're looking at one or two sides falling out of the picture late on. However, there is some drama to be found. Nashville SC tied the single-season points record last week. Any sort of result against FC Cincinnati on Saturday, and they will set a new one. And even if the West isn't all that pumping, having a number of games kick off at the same time means things will fluctuate throughout the night. So, what does this all look like? And does this year's Decision Day feel as decisive as it should? GOAL writers break it down in another edition of... The Rondo . Will Nashville SC set a points record this weekend? Callaghan might be tempted to rest some of his guys and make sure nothing goes too wrong. But their opponent, FC Cincinnati, are more or less locked where they're at. top.title: Paris FC rule out potential Lassine Sinayoko sale
top.description: Paris FC rule out potential Lassine Sinayoko sale The story of Lassine Sinayoko (26) is one of redemption. Having been turned down by numerous clubs in his youth, the Paris FC striker is now regarded as one of the best players in the French league. As Ligue 1’s top scorer (eight goals) and third-highest assist provider (five assists) this season, the Malian is making a big impression. Indeed, in the eyes of many observers, Paris FC – who signed him during the summer transfer window from AJ Auxerre for €8m – have undoubtedly pulled off one of the best deals of the recent summer transfer window. Much to the delight of the Parisian club, which, according to reports in L’Équipe , has no intention whatsoever of parting ways with Sinayoko, whose contract runs until 2029 and whose performances are, unsurprisingly, a source of complete satisfaction for the club’s management. Be that as it may, any club wishing to prise him away would certainly have to dig deep into their pockets. “His value exceeds €20m,” estimates a scout from a top-eight Premier League club. Whilst he is convinced that clubs such as Coventry City or Ipswich Town might be interested in the Bamako-born player, he points out that PFC currently holds all the cards in this matter. “When you’re a director at Paris FC these days, you can drive up the price by putting forward a simple argument: we’re not looking to sell, we don’t need to sell,” he concludes. top.title: Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen to have penalties
top.description: Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc will both have 10-place grid penalties in Sao Paulo on Sunday [Getty Images] Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will all have grid penalties at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Verstappen will start from the back of the grid while Hamilton and Leclerc will both have 10-place penalties. They join Mercedes driver George Russell in having penalties for using too many engine parts. Russell's drop is only five places. Verstappen will have an an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice. Leclerc, Hamilton and Russell have all fitted new internal combustion engines. The penalties for the Ferrari drivers are bigger than Russell's because it is the first time they have exceeded the limit of four engines per season, while Russell had already gone beyond that. Verstappen famously won the 2024 Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race. Rain is predicted overnight from Saturday into Sunday in the city this year, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day. Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035. F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo. "The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil." nigeria.title: Oyo’ll no longer depend on oil, raw materials for economic prosperity – Makinde
nigeria.description: …state targets global market for arts, crafts By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has declared its determination to move beyond dependence on conventional sources of revenue by harnessing the economic potential of arts, crafts, cultural festivals, and tourism to generate foreign exchange, attract international investments, and create employment opportunities. The government said it was working to transform Nigeria’s rich cultural heritage into commercially viable products for the global export market, positioning the creative economy as a major driver of economic growth and sustainable development. The initiative, which sought to unlock the enormous economic value of indigenous artistic expressions, traditional knowledge, and cultural assets, will be driven through the Oyo State Business Forum 2026, with the theme “Investment and Export Promotion of Arts and Crafts Business in Oyo State.” The forum is expected to bring together investors, artists, craftsmen, exporters, policymakers, and development partners to explore investment opportunities, strengthen export capacity, and expand the international market for Nigerian arts and crafts. Speaking at a press briefing to announce the forum, the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Dr. Wasiu Olatubosun, said the administration of Governor Seyi Makinde was deliberately repositioning culture beyond its traditional function as a custodian of heritage to become a productive economic sector capable of generating wealth, attracting investments, and contributing meaningfully to national development. Olatubosun, who spoke at the briefing organized in collaboration with the Oyo State Investment and Public-Private Partnership Agency (OYSIPA) at the state Secretariat, Ibadan, described Nigeria’s cultural wealth as an enormous but largely untapped economic resource that could compete favorably in the international marketplace. He maintained that traditional festivals, indigenous knowledge, artistic expressions, and locally produced crafts possessed considerable commercial value and could become major export commodities if properly researched, documented, developed, and marketed. According to him, the state government is also repositioning its cultural festivals from routine annual celebrations into internationally competitive tourism and entertainment products capable of attracting foreign visitors, investors, and members of the African diaspora. He identified the recent inscription of the Sango Festival on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as a major boost to Oyo State’s international cultural standing and an opportunity to attract greater global attention. The commissioner explained that the recognition had taken the annual festival in Oyo Town beyond its traditional geographical and cultural boundaries, making it an increasingly attractive destination for international tourists, cultural enthusiasts, and media organizations from Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

nigeria.title: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch says Trump deserved midterm defeat
nigeria.description: British Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has said United States President Donald Trump deserved to be defeated in the midterm elections, describing the setback as “entirely self-inflicted.” In an interview with The Independent , Badenoch criticised Trump’s handling of the Iran war, his trade policies and his treatment of allies. She said his approach did not reflect conservative principles. The Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, flipping at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts in a major blow to Trump’s Republican Party. Asked whether Trump deserved the defeat, Badenoch replied: “Yeah. He has not been acting in the way that I would consider conservative.” She condemned his tariffs, threats towards Canada and Greenland, and disputes with allies, saying they contradicted the conservative emphasis on free markets and better trade. “Where is the push for free markets and better trade… rather than protectionism, America first, the squabbling with allies? That’s not what conservatives do,” she said. Badenoch also criticised Trump’s personal attacks on journalists and political figures, stating that his conduct fell short of the standards expected of a statesman. “Trump is very charming in person, but you see the way that he talks about journalists, about individuals. It doesn’t meet the standards a statesman should meet – always wanting to get dirty in terms of insults and so on,” she said. She expressed particular unhappiness with Trump’s remarks about British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and described his treatment of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the White House as “awful.” On the Iran conflict, Badenoch said she understood and supported Trump’s initial decision to take military action due to concerns about Iran acquiring nuclear weapons, but questioned the lack of a clear strategy. “We don’t want them getting nuclear weapons. But where’s the plan?” she asked. Badenoch added that she would have been content if Trump had lost the 2024 presidential election to Kamala Harris. When asked which of the two candidates she preferred, she said: “I would say I like them both equally. Make of that what you will.” She further argued that Trump had squandered the broad coalition of voters that helped him win the presidency, including increased support from Latino and Black voters. “What’s the first thing he does? Tariffs, and then talking about Greenland and Canada. A lot of people were wondering, ‘What are you doing?’” she said. Badenoch became leader of the UK Conservative Party and Leader of the Opposition in November 2024. Born Olukemi Olufunto Adegoke in London in 1980 to Nigerian parents, she previously served as Business and Trade Secretary under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak. nigeria.title: Okafor strike for Leeds ends Tottenham’s winning run
nigeria.description: Leeds rode their luck to beat in-form Tottenham 1-0 on Saturday, benefiting from a controversial decision to allow Jayden Bogle to stay on the pitch after an ugly tackle on Mathys Tel. Substitute Noah Okafor was the match-winner, making an almost immediate impact after being introduced by Leeds boss Daniel Farke in the 77th minute. The home team started brightly and Spurs breathed a sigh of relief in the early minutes when VAR ruled that Mateus Fernandes had not handled the ball in the penalty area. As the first half wore on the visitors established themselves, though clear chances were at a premium. Leeds got the benefit of a contentious decision about 10 minutes before the break when Bogle caught Tel’s trailing ankle with his studs, leaving the Tottenham winger writhing on the ground in pain. After a lengthy VAR check no action was taken against Bogle, who was not even booked for the challenge, but Tel was forced off a few minutes later, hobbling off to be replaced by Dominic Solanke. Leeds had two big chances early in the second half as Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s header was blocked by Solanke before Nico Elvedi nodded wide on the follow-up. Calvert-Lewin then burst forward again but opted to pass to Ao Tanaka rather than shooting and the Japanese international skied his shot. Leeds were now on the front foot and Antonin Kinsky produced a wonderful stop after Sean Longstaff’s swivel and shot. But they got the goal their pressure deserved in the 79th minute. Harry Wilson, another substitute, controlled the ball and played it into the path of Okafor, who gave Kinsky no chance. Spurs came agonisingly close to an equaliser but goalkeeper James Trafford made a brilliant save from Jan Paul van Hecke’s header. The result ends Tottenham’s run of three straight league wins while it was the first victory in six games for Leeds, who climbed to eighth in the table. nigeria.title: 2027: Collect campaign money, but vote your conscience, Makinde tells Nigerians
nigeria.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde, has urged Nigerians to collect money offered to them by politicians during campaigns but vote according to their conscience. Makinde gave the advice during his presidential campaign flag-off in Bauchi, where he addressed supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged voters not to allow financial inducements to influence their electoral choices, insisting that accepting money from politicians should not translate into voting against their conscience. “When they bring money, it’s your money. Collect it, spend it, but vote your heart, and I know your heart is with us and with APM,” he told the gathering. The APM presidential candidate also called on Nigerians to support what he described as a national reset, arguing that economic hardship, insecurity and lack of inclusiveness in governance had made fundamental changes necessary. He questioned whether hunger among Nigerians should not prompt an economic reset, just as insecurity required a review of the country’s security architecture. Makinde further argued that the exclusion of many Nigerians from governance demanded a reset of the country’s socio-political environment. He said Nigerians dissatisfied with the state of affairs should embrace the proposed national reset, adding that the country needed a government capable of addressing public concerns with sincerity and transparency. He also appreciated Bauchi State Governor Bala Mohammed, whom he described as his national leader, the APM national chairman, and his wife for their support and encouragement. nigeria.title: FG warns public against NTI admissions, cancels 2026 NCE, degree intake
nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Ministry of Education has warned prospective students, parents and the general public against seeking admission into unauthorised National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes at the National Teachers’ Institute (NTI), Kaduna, following regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations. Consequently, all admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session have been cancelled, while the Institute has been directed to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, as it is not authorised to award NCE and university degrees. The ministry, in a statement by its Director, Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, emphasised that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), are permitted. Members of the public are therefore strongly advised not to apply, accept admission offers or make payments for such programmes. According to the statement, “The directive follows violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on 12 September 2025. The Ministry clarifies that NCE admissions must comply with applicable Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).” “The National Universities Commission (NUC) is also to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the directive on NTI’s discontinued degree-awarding arrangements,” the statement added. “To protect innocent students already enrolled, the NCCE will conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones. Eligible students may complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements, “it further added. The ministry reiterated that NTI’s statutory mandate remains teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development. This includes pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire the professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations. The ministry stressed that the intervention is intended to protect students, uphold academic standards and prevent further exposure of prospective applicants to unapproved programmes. It urged the public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before making enrolment or payment decisions. nigeria.title: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA Lagos, Oyo and Osun states each backed a different candidate in the February 25, 2023 presidential election, according to the results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: How Buhari promised me APC presidential ticket in 2022; I regret listening to him – Amaechi Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, won Lagos; Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, won Oyo, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, won Osun. What happened in Lagos? Lagos produced the closest of the three contests. Obi polled 582,454 votes (45.81 per cent), while Tinubu, the APC candidate, followed with 572,606 votes (45.04 per cent). The gap was 9,848 votes, less than one percentage point. Atiku trailed far behind with 75,750 votes (5.96 per cent), and Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, had 8,442 votes (0.66 per cent). What happened in Oyo? Oyo was not close. Tinubu polled 449,884 votes (55.58 per cent), well ahead of Atiku’s 182,977 votes (22.60 per cent). His lead of 266,907 votes was the widest of the three states. Obi came third in Oyo with 99,110 votes (12.24 per cent), and Kwankwaso had 4,095 votes (0.51 per cent). What happened in Osun? Osun was nearly as tight as Lagos. Atiku won with 354,366 votes (46.88 per cent), while Tinubu had 343,945 votes (45.50 per cent), a difference of 10,421 votes. Obi finished third with 23,283 votes, and Kwankwaso had 713 votes (0.09 per cent). What the combined figures show Added together, the results tell a story that the three winners alone do not. Tinubu won only one of the states, yet he finished first or second in all three and polled 1,366,435 votes across them. Obi, who topped the Lagos poll, totalled 704,847 votes across the three states because he fell to third in both Oyo and Osun. Atiku polled 613,093 votes, and Kwankwaso finished fourth in each state, with 13,250 votes combined. Put differently, Obi’s win came by the thinnest of margins in the most populous of the three states. But Tinubu’s lead in Oyo was large enough to leave him comfortably ahead of both rivals on the combined tally. nigeria.title: Pope Leo begins South America tour in ‘fairly good shape’
nigeria.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay, where he will celebrate a Mass on Saturday, as he began a 12-day tour of South America in “fairly good shape.” Leo’s sixth international tour takes him to the continent that helped shape his priesthood, just three weeks after surgery for a tumor on his right lung. The 71-year-old pontiff will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on one of the most intense papal trips in decades, meeting political leaders, prisoners and the poor, as well as old friends. Thousands of people, some waving yellow-and-white Vatican flags, lined the seafront of Uruguay’s capital Montevideo to greet him as he waved from a custom-made popemobile. But the crowds were relatively sparse in Latin America’s most secular country compared with Leo’s recent visits to France and Spain. Speaking in a half-empty Plaza Independencia, after being welcomed by left-wing President Yamandu Orsi, the pope lamented Uruguay’s high suicide rates — among the highest in the world — and appealed for healthcare to be “accessible to everyone.” He said the care he received after his lung cancer diagnosis made him think of the “many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis” or receive treatment. Leo will celebrate Mass on Saturday in a park in Paysandu, a city in western Uruguay, where 30,000 pilgrims are expected. He will then return to Montevideo to visit Casavalle, the neighborhood with the highest homicide rate in the capital, as well as the Catholic University and the Centenario Stadium, where he will preside over a prayer vigil for 60,000 people. Leo’s visit to Uruguay is the first to the country by a pope in nearly four decades. – In ‘fairly good shape’ – He told reporters on the plane carrying him across the Atlantic he was “in fairly good shape” following his surgery, and his advice for others facing their own cancer diagnosis was “not to be afraid.” The pontiff said he was bringing a message of “hope” to the world’s most Catholic continent. Liberal Uruguay is at odds with the Catholic Church — as well as Latin America’s new crop of conservative leaders — on issues such as same-sex marriage, abortion and euthanasia, which was legalized there last year. nigeria.title: Lagos ranks 28th among world’s 50 most dangerous cities – Survey
nigeria.description: By Sola Ogundipe Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial nerve centre and one of Africa’s busiest megacities, has been ranked among the world’s 50 most dangerous cities in 2026, placing 28th on a global crime index that raises fresh questions about urban safety, insecurity and the growing pressure on law enforcement. Lagos is the only Nigerian city on the ranking published by the “Numbeo Crime Index by City 2026” – a Serbia-based global data platform that compiles crowd-sourced information on crime safety, cost of living and quality of life across cities and countries. The list records Lagos with a crime index of 68.8, placing it in the high crime category under Numbeo’s classification. The index ranges from zero to 100, with scores above 60 classified as high and those above 80 as very high. Nigeria’s commercial capital is placed ahead of major cities including Damascus in Syria, New Orleans in the United States, San Juan in Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic. According to the survey, five South African cities occupy positions among the top eight, with Pietermaritzburg taking the first position, followed by Pretoria in second place, Johannesburg in fifth, Durban in sixth and Port Elizabeth in eighth. Caracas, Venezuela, and Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, occupy third and fourth positions respectively. Windhoek, Namibia, comes in at number 30. The figures also point to persistent safety concerns across the Americas. Brazil has five cities among the top 25, while the United States has several, including Memphis, Detroit, Baltimore, Albuquerque and St. Louis. Other cities featured in the top 50 include Kingston in Jamaica, Mexico City, Marseille in France, Manila in the Philippines, Birmingham in the United Kingdom and Houston in the United States. Numbeo’s Crime Index draws on several indicators, among them residents’ perceptions of crime, how safe they feel walking alone during the day or at night, and their experiences or concerns about robbery, mugging, car theft, burglary, physical attacks and harassment. It also considers drug-related problems, property crime, violent crime and corruption. The ranking reflects perceptions captured by Numbeo’s survey, rather than a verified ranking of reported criminal offences. It is based on surveys completed by Numbeo website visitors and not a direct count of police-recorded offences, reported criminal incidents or official national crime statistics. Numbeo processes the responses into scores ranging from zero to 100 to make comparisons between cities possible. The organisation also acknowledges that public perceptions of crime may not always correspond with official crime figures. business.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. business.title: Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine . entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. A critical part of thriving through a transition, a pivot or when you are starting over is to be honest about your limits. These could be the limits of your existing knowledge, expertise, and others. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Africa Comedy Live Brings Its Platform to Africa, Opening With an Invitation-Only Founding Gathering in Lagos
entertainment.description: Africa Comedy Live (ACL), the platform connecting African comedians, content creators and audiences across the continent and the diaspora, today announces its arrival in Africa with an invitation-only founding gathering, A Salute to Nollywood, to be held on Friday, 13 November 2026 at TRIB3 , Victoria Island, Lagos. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. Founded by Carrie Crawford, ACL has presented African comedy live in the United States since 2019 and is built on a simple conviction: Africa’s comedy deserves a world stage, and a place to call home. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.description: U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth delivering remarks at the event hosted at the Consul General’s residence in Lagos. Consulate General Lagos recently recognized the contributions of Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele at a lunch held at the height of Lagos Fashion Week 2026. The event recognized Akerele’s vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. The occasion brought together designers, entrepreneurs, and creative leaders to highlight fashion’s role in strengthening U.S.-Nigeria ties. “It’s an honor to celebrate Lagos Fashion Week 2026 with so many of Nigeria’s most talented designers and creative leaders. For 15 years, Omoyemi has built one of Africa’s premier fashion showcases, connecting Nigerian designers with American buyers and retailers and showing how trade creates opportunity for both our countries,” said U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth . In attendance was also award-winning American-born actress and producer Osas Ighodaro . Guests also experienced a new fashion themed game developed by Lagos based Maliyo Games, highlighting fashion’s growing links with technology and entertainment. For Nigeria’s fashion industry, access to the American market offers a pathway to expand the reach of Nigerian designers while offering entry points into Africa for U.S. retailers and businesses. Since founding Lagos Fashion Week in 2011, Omoyemi Akerele has built the platform into one of Africa’s leading fashion showcases. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Browns season heading into Week 9 versus the Saints: Ahead of schedule good enough?
sports.description: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Going into the season, the expectations around the Cleveland Browns were reasonably low . New coaching staff, the youngest roster in the league, uncertainty at the quarterback position, and the team just traded one of the best defensive players of this generation to Inglewood . Fast forward to early November, the Browns are 5-3 and are still in the playoff hunt in the AFC . Considering how many believed that around this time Cleveland would be in “making mock drafts” territory ( Editor’s Note: I did create one recently , just one), 5-3 is better than what anyone thought. As people will question how good the Browns are, it’s a fair process to go through. However, in this day and age, context is rarely used correctly. Going into the season, Cleveland had one of the easier schedules. In the first 8 games of the season, the Browns were only favored in 1 of their 5 wins, their most recent one: Week 2 @ Buccaneers: 23-19 Week 3 vs Panthers: 21-18 Week 4 vs Steelers: 27-24 Week 6 vs Ravens: 13-10 Week 7 @ Titans: 27-24 Fans’ confidence in the team has waxed and waned throughout the season, but is higher than it was before the season. If you want to argue which win was most impressive, you can make an argument that it was the home win against the Steelers. The final score doesn’t indicate how the game actually went. If you rewatched that game, the Browns looked like the better team throughout, and it was a surprise to everyone watching that night. Winning in the NFL is hard, and it doesn’t matter how you do it. Is Cleveland a good football team? Bad football team? Neither. Average, so far, but young. Offensively, despite their issues, they are better than last year. Having better personnel helps, but the scheme is better than last season. Defensively, the unit isn’t as dominant as last season, but it’s still regarded as one of the better units in the NFL. Progress is being shown even if the results aren’t as impressive. If the team were winless or 1-7, we would argue that the Browns are making any progress at all. Instead, the team is 5-3 and exceeding expectations. It’s possible that the team goes over their win total sooner rather than later , and it’s possible that the team is playing meaningful games towards mid-November and early December.
